questions.question_text: Which of the following is true of figure–ground organization?

options.text: Ground appears more solid than figure
It is possible to see both organizations at the same time
It is not reversible
The larger an area or shape the more likely it is to be seen as figure
Figure–ground relations can be perceived by senses other than vision

correct_answer.text: Figure–ground relations can be perceived by senses other than vision

correct_answers.text: Figure–ground relations can be perceived by senses other than vision

questions.explanation: Figure appears more solid; the smaller area is seen as figure.

questions.question_text: In the visual cortex:

options.text: If a lesion occurs at the front, the fovea will suffer a scotoma
The visual field map is upside down
The left half of the visual field is mapped on to the left side
The same region carries out both localization and recognition
Each neuron is responsible for analysing a very large region of the image

correct_answer.text: The visual field map is upside down

correct_answers.text: The visual field map is upside down

questions.explanation: A lesion at the back causes foveal scotoma; the map of the visual field is upside down and mirror reversed; localization is in the posterior parietal and recognition in the inferior temporal.

questions.question_text: Gestalt grouping determinants do not include:

options.text: Ambiguity
Proximity
Similarity
Continuation
Closure

correct_answer.text: Ambiguity

correct_answers.text: Ambiguity

questions.explanation: The determinants (b–e) proposed by Gestalt psychologists create the most stable, consistent and simple forms.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true of Gestalt grouping determinants?

options.text: They create unstable forms within a given pattern
They are not associated with reliable illusions
They have no influence on perception
They appear in audition
Targets become more difficult to find as the similarity of non-targets increases

correct_answer.text: They appear in audition

correct_answers.text: They appear in audition

questions.explanation: Stable forms are associated with reliable illusions; targets are easier to find as the similarity of non-targets increases.

questions.question_text: Monocular depth cues do not include:

options.text: Relative height
Proximity
Interposition
Linear perspective
Motion parallax

correct_answer.text: Proximity

correct_answers.text: Proximity

questions.explanation: Monocular cues also include shading and shadows.

questions.question_text: Bottom-up processes:

options.text: Are driven by a person's knowledge and expectations
Underlie the powerful effects of contexts on our perception
Help us perceive an ambiguous stimulus in more than one way
Help us recognize the shape of an object on the basis of its geon description
Play a major role in reading

correct_answer.text: Help us recognize the shape of an object on the basis of its geon description

correct_answers.text: Help us recognize the shape of an object on the basis of its geon description

questions.explanation: a, b, c and e are top-down processes.

questions.question_text: Perceptual constancy:

options.text: Enables us to determine how far away objects are
Is a result of constancy in retinal images
Makes localization difficult
Cannot be eliminated by removing the object from its background
Will not occur in senses other than vision

correct_answer.text: Enables us to determine how far away objects are

correct_answers.text: Enables us to determine how far away objects are

questions.explanation: Impressions on the retina change; perceptual constancy makes localization easy, can be eliminated, and may occur in other senses, e.g. hearing.

questions.question_text: The eye movements used in scanning a picture:

options.text: Are smooth and continuous
Ensure that different parts of the picture will fall on to the fovea
Use random fixation points
Avoid selective attention
All of the above

correct_answer.text: Ensure that different parts of the picture will fall on to the fovea

correct_answers.text: Ensure that different parts of the picture will fall on to the fovea

questions.explanation: Eye movements when scanning a picture consist of successive fixations on points that convey most information about the picture.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true of depth perception in infants?

options.text: It begins to appear at about 1 month
It is fully established by 6 months
At 2 months, nearness is signalled by binocular disparity
It is achieved with the establishment of monocular depth cues at 4 months
It will be developed enough for reaching for the nearer of two objects at around 2 months

correct_answer.text: It is fully established by 6 months

correct_answers.text: It is fully established by 6 months

questions.explanation: Depth perception begins to appear at 2–3 months; at 4 months, nearness is signalled by binocular disparity; monocular depth cues are established at 6 months; reaching for the nearer of two objects begins at 4 months.

questions.question_text: Perceptual constancy can be experienced for:

options.text: Colour
Shape
Location
Size
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Perceptual constancy is the tendency for the appearance of objects to remain constant even though their impression on the retina is changing.

questions.question_text: Cones:

options.text: Are more sensitive to light than rods
Respond to low levels of illumination
Are more numerous
Are for bright vision
Are positioned more towards the periphery of the retina

correct_answer.text: Are for bright vision

correct_answers.text: Are for bright vision

questions.explanation: a, b, c and e apply to rods.

questions.question_text: With regard to colour perception, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: People with normal vision are dichromatic
Most colour deficiencies are genetic in origin
Colour blindness occurs more frequently in males
The colour blindness gene is recessive
The colour blindness gene is located in the X chromosome

correct_answer.text: People with normal vision are dichromatic

correct_answers.text: People with normal vision are dichromatic

questions.explanation: People with normal vision are described as trichomates and they can match a wide range of colours with three primary colours. Dichromates are individuals with deficient colour vision who can match only two primary colours. Monochromates are individuals with deficient colour vision who are unable to discriminate between the different wavelengths of colours.

questions.question_text: Regarding perceptual set, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: Certain aspects of stimuli are perceived according to expectation
It is associated with a change in perception threshold
Perception is influenced by individual values
Perception is influenced by past experiences
Introverts cannot sustain attention for a long time

correct_answer.text: Introverts cannot sustain attention for a long time

correct_answers.text: Introverts cannot sustain attention for a long time

questions.explanation: Introverts can sustain attention for a long time.

questions.question_text: Gestalt psychology principles include all of the following, except:

options.text: The whole perception is the same as the sum of its parts
The percept corresponds to the simplest form in the pattern
The law of closure holds that partial outlines are perceived as whole
Adjacent items are grouped together
Figures are differentiated from ground by contours and boundaries, simulating objects

correct_answer.text: The whole perception is the same as the sum of its parts

correct_answers.text: The whole perception is the same as the sum of its parts

questions.explanation: The whole perception is different from the sum of its parts.

questions.question_text: With regard to object constancy, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: Size constancy is present in a 4-month-old infant
Moving an object from close to the face to one metre away results in no apparent change in the size of the object, but retinal image size is reduced by half
To perceive an object moving, it is necessary for the image to move across the retina
Whatever the availability of light the colour of an object can be perceived
Emmett proposed the size–distance invariance principle

correct_answer.text: To perceive an object moving, it is necessary for the image to move across the retina

correct_answers.text: To perceive an object moving, it is necessary for the image to move across the retina

questions.explanation: In stroboscopic motion and induced motion, the image does not move on the retina.

questions.question_text: With regard to perceptual stimuli for various senses:

options.text: Absolute threshold is the minimum difference in stimulus magnitude necessary to tell two stimuli apart
A just noticeable difference is the minimum magnitude of a stimulus that can be reliably discriminated from no stimulus at all
The larger the value of the standard stimulus, the less sensitive the sensory system is to changes in intensity
Weber's law states that sensory perception is a logarithmic function of stimulus intensity

Fechner's law states that the increase in stimulus intensity needed to allow two sources of intensity to be perceived as being different is directly proportional to the value of the baseline intensity

correct_answer.text: The larger the value of the standard stimulus, the less sensitive the sensory system is to changes in intensity

correct_answers.text: The larger the value of the standard stimulus, the less sensitive the sensory system is to changes in intensity

questions.explanation: (a) Just noticeable difference, (b) absolute threshold, (d) Fechner's, (e) Weber's.

questions.question_text: Regarding information processing:

options.text: Conceptually driven processing uses template matching
Data-driven processing is applied when data are incomplete
Data-driven processing uses perceptual schema
Conceptually driven data can lead to misperceptions
Data-driven processing biases the processing mechanisms to give expected results

correct_answer.text: Conceptually driven data can lead to misperceptions

correct_answers.text: Conceptually driven data can lead to misperceptions

questions.explanation: Data-driven processing uses template matching. Conceptually driven processing is applied when data are incomplete; it uses perceptual schema and biases the processing.

questions.question_text: Regarding attention, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: The right frontal lobe is essential for the maintenance of attention
In dichotic listening, the listener can switch rapidly to the unattended channel.
In divided attention, loss of performance is called dual-task interference
A defect in controlled attention might underlie symptoms of schizophrenia
For controlled attention, little conscious effort is required

correct_answer.text: For controlled attention, little conscious effort is required

correct_answers.text: For controlled attention, little conscious effort is required

questions.explanation: For automatic attention little conscious effort is required, but for controlled attention more effort is needed.

questions.question_text: Illusions:

options.text: Are less transient than hallucinations
Do not need real stimuli
Are not influenced by the perceptual set
Suggest an active search for meaning
Have no emotional component

correct_answer.text: Suggest an active search for meaning

correct_answers.text: Suggest an active search for meaning

questions.explanation: Illusions are more transient, need real stimuli, are influenced by the perceptual set, and have a strong emotional component.

questions.question_text: Disturbance of depth perception and perceptual constancy is seen in all of the following, except:

options.text: Schizophrenia
Depersonalization
Obsessive compulsive disorder
Delirium
Epilepsy

correct_answer.text: Obsessive compulsive disorder

correct_answers.text: Obsessive compulsive disorder

questions.explanation: In temporal lobe epilepsy and acute brain syndromes disturbance of perception occurs.

questions.question_text: Signal detection theory states that perception depends on all of the following, except:

options.text: Stimulus intensity
Stroop effect
Motivation
Previous experience
Expectations

correct_answer.text: Stroop effect

correct_answers.text: Stroop effect

questions.explanation: Automatic processing interferes with controlled processing.

questions.question_text: Regarding integration of hunger signals in the hypothalamus, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: A lesion in the lateral hypothalamus produces lack of hunger
A lesion in the ventromedial hypothalamus produces a voracious appetite
Morphine can suppress appetite when it is injected into the ventromedial hypothalamus
Amphetamine can suppress appetite when it is injected into the lateral hypothalamus
Lesions in the mesolimbic dopamine system mimic a lesion in the lateral hypothalamus

correct_answer.text: Morphine can suppress appetite when it is injected into the ventromedial hypothalamus

correct_answers.text: Morphine can suppress appetite when it is injected into the ventromedial hypothalamus

questions.explanation: Morphine can stimulate feeding when it is injected into the ventromedial hypothalamus.

questions.question_text: With regard to intrinsic motivation theories, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: Attachment is a result of intrinsic primary drive
High arousal leads to increased performance
Cognitive dissonance theory was first formulated by Festinger
Need for achievement theory was formulated by McClelland
If two or more inconsistent cognitions are held simultaneously, discomfort occurs

correct_answer.text: High arousal leads to increased performance

correct_answers.text: High arousal leads to increased performance

questions.explanation: High and low arousals lead to reduced performance, and moderate arousal is optimum (Yerkes–Dodson curve).

questions.question_text: With regard to intrinsic motivation theories, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: The activity engaged in has its own intrinsic reward
A moderate degree of arousal leads to an optimum degree of alertness
The Yerkes–Dodson curve is U-shaped
The individual motivated to achieve cognitive consistency may change one or more of the cognitions
When attitude and behaviour are inconsistent, the alteration of attitude brings cognitive consistency

correct_answer.text: The Yerkes–Dodson curve is U-shaped

correct_answers.text: The Yerkes–Dodson curve is U-shaped

questions.explanation: The Yerkes–Dodson curve is an inverted U-shape.

questions.question_text: Maslow's hierarchy of needs includes all of the following, except:

options.text: Self-actualization
Self-motivation
Self-esteem
Safety
Physical needs

correct_answer.text: Self-motivation

correct_answers.text: Self-motivation

questions.explanation: Love and belonging, and autonomy are also included.

questions.question_text: Regarding motivation, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: Reward is mediated by the mesolimbic dopaminergic system
Maslow's hierarchy of needs states that needs at one level should be satisfied before the next level becomes important
Gender differences are observed in need for achievement
Motivation is mainly a result of primary reinforcers
Need for achievement theory explains pleasure resulting from mastery

correct_answer.text: Motivation is mainly a result of primary reinforcers

correct_answers.text: Motivation is mainly a result of primary reinforcers

questions.explanation: Motivation is mainly a result of secondary reinforcers.

questions.question_text: Cognitive dissonance:

options.text: Is affectively neutral
Helps us find choices in uncertain situations
Decreases with personal responsibility for actions
Cannot be reduced by denying information
Is the same as attitude-discrepant behaviour

correct_answer.text: Helps us find choices in uncertain situations

correct_answers.text: Helps us find choices in uncertain situations

questions.explanation: Cognitive dissonance can cause discomfort and dysphoria, increases with personal responsibility, and can be reduced by denying information.

questions.question_text: Regarding theories of emotion, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: The James–Lange theory views the emotional response to a situation as resulting from physiological factors
The Cannon–Bard theory holds that following perception of an emotionally important event, both somatic experience and the experience of emotion occur together
Schacter's cognitive labelling theory states that emotional experience is based on cognitive appraisal of the arousal
On a Yerkes–Dodson curve the optimal level is a fixed point regardless of task complexity
According to the Schachter and Singer model, cognitive cues are important in interpretation of arousal

correct_answer.text: On a Yerkes–Dodson curve the optimal level is a fixed point regardless of task complexity

correct_answers.text: On a Yerkes–Dodson curve the optimal level is a fixed point regardless of task complexity

questions.explanation: On the Yerkes–Dodson curve the optimal level is not a fixed point and depends on many factors, including task complexity.

questions.question_text: Regarding stress:

options.text: Stimulus models take into account the person interacting with the environment
Response models view stress as the non-specific response of the body to the demands placed upon it
Response models take into account the psychological reactions to stress
The general adaptation syndrome includes alarm reaction, resistance and relaxation
In transactional models the individual is not seen as an active participant in the process of emotional appraisal

correct_answer.text: Response models view stress as the non-specific response of the body to the demands placed upon it

correct_answers.text: Response models view stress as the non-specific response of the body to the demands placed upon it

questions.explanation: Stimulus models take no account of the person interacting with the environment. Response models do not take into account the psychological reactions to stress. The general adaptation syndrome includes alarm reaction, resistance and exhaustion.

questions.question_text: Physiological reactions to stress include all of the following, except:

options.text: Increased metabolic rate
Increased heart rate
Constriction of pupil
Secretion of endorphins and ACTH
Release of extra sugar from the liver

correct_answer.text: Constriction of pupil

correct_answers.text: Constriction of pupil

questions.explanation: Pupil dilation is the physiological reaction associated with stress. Increased blood pressure also occurs in association with stress.

questions.question_text: Regarding stress, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: Positive events can be stressful
Assault victims are twice as likely to develop mental health problems at some time after the assault
The more uncontrollable the event seems, the less likely it is to be perceived as stressful
Predictability of the occurrence of a stressful event reduces the severity of the stress
Employed mothers are more likely to develop heart disease

correct_answer.text: The more uncontrollable the event seems, the less likely it is to be perceived as stressful

correct_answers.text: The more uncontrollable the event seems, the less likely it is to be perceived as stressful

questions.explanation: The more uncontrollable the event seems the more likely it is to be perceived as stressful. Employed women are not at high risk of CHD but employed mothers are at higher risk.

questions.question_text: Regarding stress, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: Type A personality was described by Friedman and Rosenman
Type A personality is related to increased proneness to heart attack
It is possible to modify type A personality
Type B personality strives for achievement with time urgency
Several studies have found that a person's level of hostility is a better predictor of heart attack than the person's overall level of type A behaviour

correct_answer.text: Type B personality strives for achievement with time urgency

correct_answers.text: Type B personality strives for achievement with time urgency

questions.explanation: Type A personality: competitiveness, difficulty relaxing, impatience, anger, striving for achievement with time urgency.

questions.question_text: Regarding locus of control, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: It was proposed by Rotter
The more anxious or depressed a person, the more internal his or her locus of control tends to be
A greater external locus of control is associated with a greater vulnerability to physical illness
With successful therapeutic intervention locus of control can be changed
Biofeedback aims to change the physiological state directly

correct_answer.text: The more anxious or depressed a person, the more internal his or her locus of control tends to be

correct_answers.text: The more anxious or depressed a person, the more internal his or her locus of control tends to be

questions.explanation: The more anxious or depressed a person, the more external his or her locus of control tends to be.

questions.question_text: The following defence mechanisms used to cope with stress are all correctly matched, except:

options.text: Denial–Concentration only on the current task
Repression–Suppression of inappropriate feelings
Isolation–Objectivity
Projection–Empathy
Rationalization–Substitution of other thoughts for disturbing ones

correct_answer.text: Rationalization–Substitution of other thoughts for disturbing ones

correct_answers.text: Rationalization–Substitution of other thoughts for disturbing ones

questions.explanation: Rationalization–Logical analysis; Reaction formation–Substitution of other thoughts for disturbing ones.

questions.question_text: Regarding learned helplessness:

options.text: It was proposed by Rotter
Those who believe nobody could have controlled the outcome of the event are more likely to develop learned helplessness
Locus of control theory is largely based on this concept
It develops regardless of a person's attribution
It may explain why some women remain in abusive relationships even when they have opportunities to leave

correct_answer.text: It may explain why some women remain in abusive relationships even when they have opportunities to leave

correct_answers.text: It may explain why some women remain in abusive relationships even when they have opportunities to leave

questions.explanation: Learned helplessness was proposed by Seligman. Those who believe nobody could have controlled the outcome of the event are less likely to develop learned helplessness, while those who believe they have personal control over the event are more likely to develop learned helplessness; the cognitive theory of depression is largely based on this concept.

questions.question_text: In memory:

options.text: The regions in the right hemisphere of the brain are activated during encoding
The regions in the left hemisphere of the brain are activated during retrieval
Immediate memory and working memory are synonymous
Short-term memory has a duration of 20 seconds unless it is rehearsed
Sensory or iconic memory plays a major role in thought and conscious recollection

correct_answer.text: Short-term memory has a duration of 20 seconds unless it is rehearsed

correct_answers.text: Short-term memory has a duration of 20 seconds unless it is rehearsed

questions.explanation: The right hemisphere of the brain is used for retrieval; the left hemisphere is used for encoding; iconic memory plays far less of a role in thought and conscious recollection.

questions.question_text: With regard to brain regions involved in memory:

options.text: The hippocampus is critical for long-term memory and working memory
The frontal cortex is critical for long-term memory
People with medial temporal lobe damage have severe amnesia and have difficulty remembering material for more than a few seconds
People with medial temporal lobe damage have severe amnesia and have difficulty recognizing familiar people
People with medial temporal lobe damage have an abnormal working memory

correct_answer.text: People with medial temporal lobe damage have severe amnesia and have difficulty recognizing familiar people

correct_answers.text: People with medial temporal lobe damage have severe amnesia and have difficulty recognizing familiar people

questions.explanation: The hippocampus is critical for long-term memory only and not for working memory. The frontal cortex is critical in working memory. Medial temporal lobe damage does not affect working memory.

questions.question_text: In human memory, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: Encoding is mainly acoustic
Visual encoding rapidly fades
Sensory memory is long lived
Haptic memory is a sensory memory
Sensory memory is retained in an unprocessed form in peripheral receptors

correct_answer.text: Sensory memory is long lived

correct_answers.text: Sensory memory is long lived

questions.explanation: Sensory memory is short lived.

questions.question_text: In working memory, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: Rehearsal facilitates phonological coding
Eidetic memory occurs mainly in children
Acoustic and visual–spatial buffers are mediated by the same brain structures
The capacity of working memory is 7 +2
Chunking improves the capacity of working memory

correct_answer.text: Acoustic and visual–spatial buffers are mediated by the same brain structures

correct_answers.text: Acoustic and visual–spatial buffers are mediated by the same brain structures

questions.explanation: Acoustic buffer is mediated by the left hemisphere; visual–spatial buffers are mediated by the right hemisphere.

questions.question_text: Regarding working memory, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: It can be boosted by regrouping
It can be boosted by displacement
It can be boosted by chunking
It can be boosted by rehearsing
Forgetting may occur due to decay

correct_answer.text: It can be boosted by displacement

correct_answers.text: It can be boosted by displacement

questions.explanation: Displacement is a cause of forgetting.

questions.question_text: About memory, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: The recency effect is remembering easily the most recent words encountered from a list of words
The primacy effect is retrieving the first words on a word list
Both primacy and recency effects are involved in remembering a list of words
The serial position effect is retrieving the last few words on a word list
The recency effect is explained by the short time elapsed before recall

correct_answer.text: The serial position effect is retrieving the last few words on a word list

correct_answers.text: The serial position effect is retrieving the last few words on a word list

questions.explanation: Serial position effect means that items from the intermediate position are least likely to be recalled.

questions.question_text: Regarding short-term memory:

options.text: Encoding is mainly acoustic
Verbal short-term memory is stored in the left hemisphere and visual short-term memory is stored in the right hemisphere
Retrieval is effortless and error free
Short-term memory has an average limit of seven pieces of information
All of the above are true

correct_answer.text: All of the above are true

correct_answers.text: All of the above are true

questions.explanation: Short-term memory is temporary working memory; it is lost in 20 seconds unless it is rehearsed; it uses the principles of displacement, chunking, primacy effect, recency effect and eidetic memory.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true of semantic memory?

options.text: It is a long-term memory for events
It is autobiographical in nature
It is stored in terms of meaning
Semantic encoding is less efficient than rehearsal
It is continually changing

correct_answer.text: It is stored in terms of meaning

correct_answers.text: It is stored in terms of meaning

questions.explanation: a, b and e apply to episodic memory.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true of forgetting?

options.text: It is mainly caused by storage failure
Retrieval failure can explain the 'tip-of-the-tongue' experience
Forgetting by interference is not item dependent
Forgetting by decay is item dependent
All of the above

correct_answer.text: Retrieval failure can explain the 'tip-of-the-tongue' experience

correct_answers.text: Retrieval failure can explain the 'tip-of-the-tongue' experience

questions.explanation: Forgetting is mainly due to retrieval failure; forgetting by interference is item dependent and by decay is time dependent.

questions.question_text: With regard to language units and processes, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: All languages have the same set of phonemes
Morpheme refers to any small linguistic unit that carries meaning
Words, prefixes and suffixes are examples of morphemes
Over the first year of life children learn which phonemes are relevant to their language and lose their ability to discriminate between other phonemes.
The first step in extracting propositions from a complex sentence is to deconstruct the sentence into phrases

correct_answer.text: All languages have the same set of phonemes

correct_answers.text: All languages have the same set of phonemes

questions.explanation: Every language has a different set of phonemes. A phoneme is a speech sound. The English language has 40 phonemes.

questions.question_text: Regarding the development of language:

options.text: Children learn language by imitating adults
Children acquire language through conditioning
Children form a hypothesis about a rule of language, test it and retain it if it works
There is indirect evidence for the existence of a critical period for language acquisition, in the case of children who have experienced extreme isolation
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Research has shown that there is a critical period for learning syntax.

questions.question_text: As a building block of thought, concept:

options.text: Represents an entire class
Is an example of the brain's ability to reduce information-processing load
Allows prediction
May include physical objects
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Categorization refers to the process of assigning an object to a concept.

questions.question_text: Prototypes:

options.text: Are the most logical and strictly accurate examples of a member of a concept
Represent the most popular and best recognized example
Cannot be accessed easily
Are a more perfect indicator of the concept than its core properties
Are not universal

correct_answer.text: Represent the most popular and best recognized example

correct_answers.text: Represent the most popular and best recognized example

questions.explanation: Prototypes are not necessarily logical or even strictly accurate examples of a member of a concept, but represent the most popular and best recognized example. They can be accessed easily, and are highly salient examples of a concept, but these properties are not necessarily conditions for concept membership, whereas the core properties are more central to concept membership. For some concepts culture has a major impact on the prototype, but for more natural concepts prototypes are surprisingly universal.

questions.question_text: About acquiring concepts, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: Explicit teaching is likely to be the means by which we learn cores of concepts
Experience seems to be the usual means by which we acquire prototypes
Five-year-old children show a clear shift from the prototype to the core as the final arbitrator of concept decisions
Prior knowledge may affect every aspect of concept attainment
Research shows that prototype-based categorization does not depend on the brain structures that mediate long-term memory

correct_answer.text: Five-year-old children show a clear shift from the prototype to the core as the final arbitrator of concept decisions

correct_answers.text: Five-year-old children show a clear shift from the prototype to the core as the final arbitrator of concept decisions

questions.explanation: Not until age 10 do children show a clear shift from the prototype to the core as the final arbitrator of concept decisions.

questions.question_text: In reasoning, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: In deductively valid arguments, it is impossible for the conclusion of the argument to be false if its premises are true
Inductive reasoning is probabilistic
An algorithm, if applied stepwise, will always guarantee the solution to a problem
Heuristics invariably yield the correct answer
Heuristic arguments depend on cognitive short-cuts such as prototypes

correct_answer.text: Heuristics invariably yield the correct answer

correct_answers.text: Heuristics invariably yield the correct answer

questions.explanation: A heuristic procedure is a short-cut that is relatively easy to apply and can often yield the correct answer, but not invariably so.
